mainEvent.title: Fri 11/27 · A half-day rally caps a 5.6% rebound week for the S&P 500
mainEvent.body: Stocks bounced hard in the holiday-shortened week after the S&P 500 fell into a correction on Nov 20: the S&P 500 gained about **5.6%**, the Nasdaq **6.7%**, the Dow 5.5% and the Russell 2000 6.5% (Vista Partners, AP via Political.org). Monday's surge on Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia (S&P 500 +4.7%, its best day since April 2025) gave way to two days of chip selling, including a steep Wednesday morning drop on hot core PCE (3.3%) and new tariff proposals, before Friday's half-day rally: S&P 500 **+1.60%** to 7,297.49, Nasdaq **+2.31%** to 24,129.50. The VIX fell to 23.81 from 35.89 a week earlier (Cboe), but CNN's Fear & Greed is still in extreme fear at 25. Next: OPEC+ meets Sunday, the Fed's pre-meeting blackout starts Saturday with a 25bp hike on Dec 9 almost fully priced, job openings are out Tue 12/1, and Nvidia's 10-Q is due Dec 4.

stories.title: A half-day Black Friday rally caps a big rebound week as chips bounce and Anthropic climbs back above its IPO price.
stories.body: The S&P 500 rose **1.60%** to 7,297.49, the Nasdaq **2.31%** to 24,129.50, the Dow 1.18% (+591.99) to 50,774.94 and the Russell 2000 1.71% to 2,750.30 in a session that ended at 1:00p (Vista Partners, AP via Political.org, ad-hoc-news). For the week the S&P 500 gained about **5.6%**, the Nasdaq **6.7%**, the Dow 5.5% and the Russell 2000 6.5%, after the S&P 500 fell into a correction on Nov 20; Vista Partners calls it the Dow's best week since October 2022. Chips led again after China's chip index posted its biggest one-day gain on record (CNBC via StockTitan, Vista Partners): Sandisk rose **16%**, Micron 7.6% and Nvidia 0.8% to $150.49, still 8.8% below Monday's close (StockTitan). Amazon gained about 4% and Meta and Broadcom about 3–4% (Vista Partners, AP via Political.org). Anthropic (**ANT**) jumped **11%** to $91.88, back above its $83 IPO price (StockTitan, Vista Partners). All 11 sector funds rose, led by tech (XLK) +2.8% (sector ETFs). Vertex fell 5.2% after the FDA pushed its povetacicept decision to Feb 28, and Alvotech 12% after a US court blocked its Simponi copy (StockTitan). The VIX fell 11% to 23.81 (Cboe), while the 10Y rose about 9bp to 4.93%. Bloomberg reported that Nvidia Blackwell chips barred from China were installed at a Shanghai data center (via StockTitan). Polymarket's odds of Nvidia ending 2026 above $4T with Huang as CEO are about 36%; its 10-Q is due Dec 4.

stories.title: Core PCE runs hot at 3.3%, GDP is revised up to 4.3% and new home sales jump 14%, keeping a December hike priced.
stories.body: October core PCE rose **0.3%** on the month as expected but **3.3%** on the year, above the 3.2% forecast and up from 3.1%; headline PCE rose 3.8% as expected and personal income jumped 0.7% (BEA via Unusual Whales, PANews). Q3 GDP was revised up to **4.3%** from 3.4%, durable goods rose 0.2% vs about 0.5% expected, and jobless claims fell to 189K (Breaking The News, InstaForex). New home sales jumped **14.2%** to a 701,000 rate in October vs 650,000 expected, the most since December 2025, though September was revised down to 614,000 from 676,000; the median price fell 3.2% from a year earlier to $391,300 and supply fell to 8.0 months (Commerce Department via Reuters/WHBL, Anadolu). The Fed's Beige Book said 8 of 12 districts grew slightly to moderately and 4 were flat; "prices increased moderately overall," input costs "generally outpaced" selling prices, and wages rose moderately, "an uptick" from the prior report (Federal Reserve). The 10Y fell about 6bp to 4.85% Wednesday, then rose back to about 4.93% Friday as stocks rallied. CME FedWatch had about 95% on a 25bp hike on December 9 as of Tuesday (Yahoo Finance); Kalshi has 25bp at **94%**, a hold at 5% and a bigger hike at 3% (Fri 11/27 close). The pre-meeting blackout starts Saturday.

stories.title: Oil posts its first weekly gain of November after a projectile hits Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery.
stories.body: Brent for January settled at **$95.44** on Friday, down 1.2%, but rose about 3% on the week, snapping a three-week losing streak; WTI settled at **$83.08**, down 0.7% from Wednesday and 0.9% for the week (Bloomberg via Rigzone, Political.org). There was no Thursday settlement because of Thanksgiving. Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery temporarily halted some operations after a projectile struck it Thursday, killing a worker, Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry said; it followed claimed Houthi attacks on Ras Tanura (Reuters via rallies.ai, Political.org). Tankers in and around the Strait of Hormuz were attacked again this week, though traffic has stayed resilient according to Vortexa ship tracking, and a Ukrainian drone strike set a Russian refinery in the Krasnodar region on fire (Bloomberg via Rigzone, Reuters via rallies.ai). Oil is still down nearly 20% in November (Political.org). OPEC+ meets Sunday, Nov 29, and is set to keep its first-quarter 2027 output targets unchanged, three people with knowledge of the talks told Reuters.

stories.title: Brazilian assets surge as Lula picks Bradesco chairman Luiz Carlos Trabuco as finance minister.
stories.body: Trabuco, 75, Bradesco's chairman and its CEO from 2009 to 2018, accepted Lula's invitation on Thursday after meeting him in Brasília (Reuters via KELO); Bradesco said in a filing he will take the job starting in 2027 (StockTitan). Citi called the pick a sign of a "somewhat more market-friendly approach" after markets fell on Lula's October election win over Flavio Bolsonaro, who had promised deep spending cuts; public debt is near 83% of GDP and the policy rate is 13.75% (Reuters). The real strengthened as much as **4.7%** to 5.47 per dollar Friday before trading around 5.55, from about 5.88 on Wednesday, and the Bovespa rose as much as 3.9% after jumping 6% Thursday (Reuters via KELO, The Company Chronicle). In New York the Brazil fund (EWZ) rose **9.8%**, XP **18%**, Bradesco 15% and Inter&Co about 16%, and Petrobras was up 13% before the open (StockTitan). Analysts expect Trabuco to push further pension reform and revisit indexation (Reuters).

stories.title: Black Friday spending is tracking higher online, with Adobe forecasting a record $12.9B.
stories.body: Adobe Analytics expects US shoppers to spend a record **$12.9B** online on Black Friday, up 9.2% from $11.8B last year, and $15.1B on Cyber Monday; online spending from Nov 1 to 22 was **$82.5B**, up 9.1% (Adobe via roic.ai, Vista Partners). Adobe's actual tally is due Saturday. The NRF expects 182.7 million people to shop over the Thanksgiving weekend, down from 202.9 million last year (via roic.ai). Vista Partners says shoppers are favoring Walmart and Costco, while Gap lowered its outlook and Gap and TJX flagged warm weather as a drag. Consumer discretionary (XLY) rose 2.1% Friday and Amazon about 4% (sector ETFs, Vista Partners). The catch is inflation: core PCE is running at 3.3% and AAA says gas prices are up about 18% from a year ago (Vista Partners).

stories.title: The administration proposes new tariffs on 16 trading partners, with 20% on China.
stories.body: The US Trade Representative proposed new duties on 16 major trading partners after an investigation into industrial subsidies and excess manufacturing capacity: **20%** on China and **15%** on the European Union, Japan, South Korea and Taiwan, with other rates for Southeast Asian exporters (MarketScreener, StockTitan, Vista Partners). Semiconductors, autos, steel and aluminum are excluded, and the duties aren't expected before January; the US-China trade truce runs out Jan 10 (Vista Partners). Public comments are due Jan 5 and hearings start Jan 25 (StockTitan). MarketScreener says the duties are meant to replace tariffs the Supreme Court struck down earlier this year. The proposal added to the morning selling, but stocks recovered most of the losses by the close; sources differed on some smaller countries' rates, so only the figures they agree on are shown here.
